recipes.name: Italian Vegetable Soup
ingredients_raw: 1 (14.5 ounce) can peeled and diced tomatoes
2 (19 ounce) cans kidney beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Place ground beef in a large soup pot. Cook over medium heat until evenly browned. Drain excess fat. Stir in onion, celery, carrots, garlic, chopped tomatoes, tomato sauce, beans, water and bouillon. Season with parsley, oregano and basil. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in cabbage, corn, green beans and pasta. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat. Simmer until vegetables are tender and pasta is al dente. Add more water if needed.

raw_recipe.headline: Italian Vegetable Soup
raw_recipe.description: Carrots, celery, onions, cabbage, corn, and green beans -- this soup is full of vegetables! With ground beef, beans, and macaroni, a loaf of warm, crusty bread is all you need for a well-rounded dinner.

review.reviewBody: Absolutely delicious and turns out great everytime! I made without the corn because I didn't have any, but don't make any substitutions or leave out anything else, the flavors just blend to make a wonderful soup/stew. I also simmer my soup longer than the recipe calls for. Since the macaroni tends to get too mushy if you have lots of leftovers,or have to keep it simmering for awhile. I cook and drain the pasta and just add a little to each bowl as I serve it. Then refrigerate the leftover pasta and soup in seperate containers. This is so great and different from stew or chili. I made it when I had out of town guests flying in and wasn't sure when they would arrive. They got to our home and were so happy to be met with the delightful smell and be served this satisfying and hearty soup with french bread and a fresh fruit salad after a long and hungry flight!

This soup is very good. If you want this soup to taste like the Italian soup served at the Olive Garden, try these changes - Supplement the water for two 12 oz. boxes of beef stock, and add three boullion cubes.

This made so much soup, way more than 8 servings. I substituted kale for the cabbage, though I plan to use the cabbage next time. I also used 32 oz of beef broth, and a tablespoon of "beef - better than broth" instead of the water. I did not make the pasta, I'm trying to watch carbs, and honestly, I didn't miss them at all, this is packed with vegetables. This is a fabulous recipe, and I can see using all sorts of variations. Excellent.

Excellent - As a vegan I had to made a few changes. I substituted Soy crumbles for the beef, vegetable bouillon for the beef bouillon. I also used a large 28oz can of fire roasted crushed tomatoes and 8oz can of sauce and I added extra garlic, of course. This was definitely a hit with the whole family! A great soup to freeze for later lunches and dinners, I didn't add pasta until I was ready to serve since pasta gets too soft when frozen. Thanks for passing this along!

I thought this was great. Taking the suggestion of so many, I added more water - 3 cups worth - and I used 3 beef bouillon cubes in total. I drained both the corn and kidney beans before putting them in and only used 1 can of beans. I used fresh french green beans...AND...I did the whole thing in the slow cooker. I started real late on this, at 3pm and I put it on high. I was finished chopping everything up and threw it all in by 3:30pm. Since time was going to be tight, I put it on high as I was throwing everything in to get it started. By 7:30pm, although the veggies weren't completely done, we had dinner ready. It's still in the crock pot now actually and I'm giving it another hour total. It was a really great and very healthy meal. I will definitely make it again! Super easy, too.

Love this soup! I make the macaroni on the side so it doesn't soak up all the juice. I also cheat on chopping the vegetables. I use three 10 oz. bags of frozen Birds Eye Steamfresh Mixed Vegetables and a 10 oz bag of fresh Angel Hair Coleslaw.

I have always loved my mother's vegetable soup recipe but this is a much easier recipe and tastes almost the same! My only change was that I sautéed the mirepoix first in a little olive oil until the onion was translucent then added the garlic for 30 seconds before adding the beef. After draining some of the fat (not much since I used 90% lean), I added the rest of the ingredients in Step 1, opting to use beef broth instead of water and bouillon. I then let it simmer for about an hour and a half. I added the cabbage and green beans during the last 15 minutes (omitted the corn because of a family food allergy) and cooked the pasta separately (so that I could control the doneness) adding that just before serving. I did not have to adjust any of the seasonings except I did use a little salt and pepper since I used all low-sodium canned ingredients. After reading the other reviews, I agree that you have to use more liquid. I started out with 2-3 cups of broth then ended up adding another 2 ½ cups towards the end. It is more like a stew that a soup but totally delicious and very hearty. This is not a wimpy vegetable soup!

I made some changes based on other reviewers and what I had in the pantry. I used ground turkey, which I cooked in a skillet with the onions and garlic. I also used a 14 ounce can of beef broth instead of the water and bouillon granules. I put in part of a bag of coleslaw for the cabbage and omitted the macaroni. I threw everything in my crockpot and cooked it on high for almost 4 hours. (I waited to put the cabbage in at the end). We loved the taste, however my husband would have liked more tomato flavor. Next time I would add two cans of tomatoes. I will make this again and omit the ground turkey to make it even healthier.

Loved it! Used Herbox beef instant bouillon. Lightly sauteed the celery, onion, carrots and garlic before adding to the soup pot. Used fresh green beans (had them in the fridge) Didn't use the corn or cabbage (didn't have them available). It was so delicious!! And I agree with another reviewer - tastes a lot like Olive Garden soups (which I like, especially their pasta e fagioli soup.

I love this soup! I make it in the winter on cold days with whatever veggies I have lying around. This time I added zucchini, canned mushrooms and peas, along with most of the other items listed in the recipe. It turned out great! I usually make it in bulk and then store the leftovers in small containers to defrost and have for dinner during a busy week. My kids especially love it. I usually cook the noodles separately though because they soak up so much of the water. Highly recommended!

Great recipe however I made a few changes. I used a 24oz box of beer stock instead of the water and bouillon. I used frozen and fresh veggies- no cans except for pinto beans. I cooked it all in crockpot for six hours then added cabbage. Served macaroni on side to cut the cards for those of us who are dieting.

The first time I made this recipe I made it as written. I don’t care for the commenters that make a TON of changes and then write reviews. Just make your own recipe. The first time I made this, the only change I made was more than doubling the water and spices, and I did that out of necessity as without doing so, this isn’t a soup. I probably use 4 cups of beef broth and 1-2 cups of water and that’s without draining the corn and beans. This is a fantastic soup with all the vegetables and base spices, but I now use beef broth instead of bouillon and then I season with extra salt. I also use pepper and onion powder. Sometimes I use kale or spinach if I don’t have cabbage. You can use whatever veggies you want! Family loves it with a crusty bread and butter.
Recipe is easy to follow and my family loves this soup!
Simple and tasty. Added butter and salt and still needed more flavor for me, but just right for husband.

This soup is fantastic! I was under the weather and my husband made this. We made it exactly as directed except we added a 32 ounce carton of low sodium beef broth in lieu of the water. We let it summer for several hours. It is fantastic vegetable soup. Thank you so much for this recipe.

Definitely a keeper! I've been waiting for cooler weather to come to Central Ohio before making this, but I got tired of waiting. I only made 2 changes. I used leftover roast beef. I've never been a fan of using ground beef in soup recipes. I substituted the water for beef broth. I made a loaf of good, crusty bread to go with it. My husband asked me to double the recipe next time, and it's only the two of us. This recipe is the bomb!
Took a little time for chopping and opening cans (LOL) but it's definitely a favorite!!
Very good. Wouldn’t change a thing.
Cook Manual for 5 minutes in Instant Pot. I use Knorr beef bouillon and it’s delicious.
Great flavor. I subbed some leftover roast beef for hamburger, otherwise followed the recipe.
